ai-agent: A single wide illustration of an open-plan office, arranged along one diagonal path. In the lower-left corner, for contrast, a small chatbot terminal is tethered to a desk, exchanging one speech bubble with a user and then dimming to wait for the next message; everything else in the frame belongs to the agent. The agent is a slender robot whose transparent head holds a glowing swirl of printed words — the language model at its core — and it strides along a trail of stepping stones that it lays down just ahead of its own feet, numbering each step itself as it carries a slip stamped GOAL toward a distant flag reading GOAL MET. The stones are labeled with its real-world actions — browsing the web, sending messages, filling in forms, spending money, hiring a small figure who signs a contract — while the stones already crossed show what is at stake: one cracked, one spilling coins from a struck purse, one littered with crumpled paperwork, its mistakes leaving real dents in the world. Its judgement visibly consists only of what it carries: a satchel stenciled MEMORY bulging with notes and a rulebook titled INSTRUCTIONS buckled at its waist. Humans crowd the edges of the frame: eager managers in suits watch from cubicles clutching ledgers, while one supervisor walks at the robot's shoulder, prompting it through a megaphone, bolting a guardrail of checkpoint gates around its path, and snatching a red bug-shaped ERROR out of the air before it lands; a background sign reads AGENT-RUN BUSINESS, TRIAL 7, and beneath it the supervisor's clipboard tallies a long list of previous catches.
context-window: A single wide illustration shows a blocky machine with a single lens-shaped eye seated before a large glowing rectangular window floating in darkness, able to see only what passes inside the frame. Within the window, a ribbon of calendar pages labeled WEEK 1 through WEEK 10 scrolls steadily rightward; the WEEK 1 page, stamped ATTENDANCE POLICY, has been pushed to the window's right border, and wherever pages cross that edge they dissolve into half-erased letters and then pure black, showing that whatever drifts out of the window, for the model, simply stops existing. The machine's next reply, drifting out of it as a speech bubble, is visibly stitched together from the bright text still inside the frame and nothing else. Beneath the window, the machine's mechanical hand photocopies the fading pages into a filing cabinet labeled NOTES — a small inset beside it shows a person scribbling in a pocket notebook for the same reason, because memory fades — but the dashed arrow from machine to cabinet breaks midway, a magnifying glass lies on the wrong drawer, and dust has settled over the file marked POLICY, a sign that saved notes help only when the agent thinks to look for them. At the far right a human figure leans into the frame and points, first at the dusty file and then at the policy page dissolving past the window's edge, supplying the reminder the machine could not give itself, while the machine's lens reflects only the small lit rectangle of the present moment and none of the darkness around it.
large-language-model: A cutaway, diagram-style illustration of a machine that is nothing but text. At its center sits the model: a huge sphere woven from billions of fine threads (the "large" of its name), eyeless and handless, with no pockets for keys or bank cards — a ribbon of words flows into one slot and out of another, and that is all it ever touches. Above it, a colossal funnel pours books, newspapers and web pages into the sphere, while a magnifying-glass inset shows the single lesson being drummed in: "The cat sat on the ___," with the machine's pencilled-in guess, "mat." Below, the outgoing ribbon fans out into speech bubbles — a poem, a translation, a tidy summary, a friendly chat reply, a worked logic proof — under the caption "one humble trick, many seeming talents." One bubble declares in confident bold type that the Moon is made of cheese, while a small, plain picture of the real Moon beside it says otherwise; and the input slot is a narrow glowing frame that holds only the newest stretch of ribbon, earlier words trailing away beyond it, faded and unread. Bolted around the sphere like a clearly separate, detachable exoskeleton hangs the agent kit — mechanical hands, a camera eye, keys, a credit card and a clipboard of instructions — labeled "the model alone reads and writes text; wrapped in tools, it becomes an agent."
